We need to write a resume for Matthias Algiers. Use words with all capital letters to highlight key abilities, but ensure that words with all capital letters appear less than 10 times. So we can use maybe 5-7 uppercase words. Must wrap the entire response with double quotation marks. That means the output should be a string enclosed in double quotes. Inside we can have line breaks? Typically if we wrap entire response with double quotation marks, we need to start with a double quote and end with a double quote, and everything inside is the content. If we include line breaks inside the quotes, that's okay as a multi-line string? Usually they'd expect a single line? Safer to put everything inside one line within quotes. But a resume usually multi-line; we can embed newline characters \n inside the string? Might be okay. However typical answer: they want the whole response wrapped with double quotation marks, meaning the output starts with " and ends with ". Inside we can have line breaks? Might be considered part of the string. Usually they'd accept multi-line inside quotes? Not sure. To be safe, produce a single-line resume with sections separated by " | " or similar. Use uppercase words for key abilities, less than 10 times. Let's pick maybe 6 uppercase words: LEADERSHIP, PROJECT_MANAGEMENT, DATA_ANALYSIS, PROBLEM_SOLVING, COMMUNICATION, TECHNICAL_SKILLS. Ensure each is uppercase and appears maybe once each. That's 6 uppercase words, less than 10. Ensure no other words are all caps inadvertently. Avoid other all caps like "AND" or "THE". Must watch not to accidentally have words like "EXPERIENCE" in caps. So keep all other words normal case.

We need to write resume: name, contact, summary, experience, education, skills. Use uppercase words only for key abilities. We'll embed them in the skills section maybe.

Make sure not to accidentally have uppercase words like "USA" or "GPA". Avoid those. Use lowercase for those.

Let's craft:

"Matthias Algiers
Email: matthias.algiers@example.com | Phone: (555) 123-4567 | LinkedIn: linkedin.com/in/matthiasalgiers
PROFESSIONAL SUMMARY
Dynamic professional with LEADERSHIP and PROJECT_MANAGEMENT expertise, skilled in DATA_ANALYSIS and PROBLEM_SOLVING, dedicated to delivering results through effective COMMUNICATION and TECHNICAL_SKILLS.
EXPERIENCE
Senior Analyst, XYZ Corp, 2020-Present
- Led cross-functional teams to improve operational efficiency by 15%
- Managed project timelines and budgets, ensuring on-time delivery
- Conducted DATA_ANALYSIS to inform strategic decisions
Project Coordinator, ABC Inc, 2017-2020
- Coordinated multiple projects simultaneously, applying PROJECT_MANAGEMENT best practices
- Facilitated stakeholder COMMUNICATION to align objectives
- Developed PROBLEM_SOLVING frameworks that reduced issue resolution time by 20%
EDUCATION
Bachelor of Science in Business Administration, University of Example, 2017
SKILLS
LEADERSHIP, PROJECT_MANAGEMENT, DATA_ANALYSIS, PROBLEM_SOLVING, COMMUNICATION, TECHNICAL_SKILLS"

Now count uppercase words: LEADERSHIP, PROJECT_MANAGEMENT, DATA_ANALYSIS, PROBLEM_SOLVING, COMMUNICATION, TECHNICAL_SKILLS. That's 6. Ensure no other all caps like "XYZ" (that's uppercase but it's an acronym; it's all caps, counts as a word with all capital letters. That would add more. We need less than 10 total uppercase words. "XYZ" is uppercase; "ABC" also uppercase; "USA"? Not present. Also "Inc" is not all caps. "Corp" not all caps. "University" not all caps. "Example" not all caps. "Email" not all caps. "Phone" not all caps. "LinkedIn" has capital L and I but not all caps. "PROFESSIONAL" appears as a heading? I wrote "PROFESSIONAL SUMMARY". That's two words: PROFESSIONAL and SUMMARY both all caps. That adds more. We must avoid any other all caps words. So we need to avoid headings in all caps. Use normal case headings. Also avoid "XYZ" and "ABC". Could use lowercase or normal case like "Xyz Corp". But company names often capitalized but we can write "Xyz Corp" (capital X, lower yz) not all caps. Similarly "Abc Inc". So we need to avoid any all caps sequences.

Thus we must ensure that the only all caps words are the six we intend for key abilities. All other words must not be all caps. So we need to avoid any other all caps like "USA", "GPA", "PDF", etc. Also avoid headings in all caps. Use normal case headings like "Professional Summary", "Experience", "Education", "Skills". Also avoid "Email:" etc. "Email:" is not all caps because "Email" capital E but lower rest; that's fine (not all caps). "Phone:" similar. "LinkedIn:" not all caps.

We need to watch for "CEO" etc none.

Thus rewrite with proper case.

Now check for any accidental all caps:

- "Matthias" normal.
- "Algiers" normal.
- "Email:" capital E but not all caps.
- "matthias.algiers@example.com" lower.
- "Phone:" capital P not all caps.
- "(555) 123-4567" numbers.
- "LinkedIn:" capital L and I but not all caps.
- "linkedin.com/in/matthiasalgiers" lower.
- "Professional Summary": both words capital first letter only, not all caps.
- "Dynamic professional with LEADERSHIP and PROJECT_MANAGEMENT expertise, skilled in DATA_ANALYSIS and PROBLEM_SOLVING, dedicated to delivering results through effective COMMUNICATION and TECHNICAL_SKILLS." Here we have LEADERSHIP, PROJECT_MANAGEMENT, DATA_ANALYSIS, PROBLEM_SOLVING, COMMUNICATION, TECHNICAL_SKILLS. All caps exactly six.
- "Experience": capital E only.
- "Senior Analyst, Xyz Corp, 2020-Present": "Xyz" capital X only; "Corp" capital C only. Good.
- Bullets: "Led", "Managed", "Conducted". "Conducted" then "DATA_ANALYSIS": that's all caps, counts as one of the six (we already counted). Good.
- "Project Coordinator, Abc Inc, 2017-2020": "Abc" capital A only; "Inc" capital I only.
- Bullets: "Coordinated", "Facilitated", "Developed". Then "PROJECT_MANAGEMENT", "COMMUNICATION", "PROBLEM_SOLVING". All caps counted.
- "Education": capital E only.
- "Bachelor of Science in Business Administration, University of Example, 2017": "Bachelor", "Science", "Business", "Administration", "University", "Example". Only first letters capital. Good.
- "Skills": capital S only.
- Then list: "LEADERSHIP, PROJECT_MANAGEMENT, DATA_ANALYSIS, PROBLEM_SOLVING, COMMUNICATION, TECHNICAL_SKILLS". Those are the six.

Thus total all caps words = 6 (<10). Good.
